Please use at least 200 characters.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake
prompt_mistake.prompt:
# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

Did you make any mistakes in remembering the names you gave to the images?

If so, please describe what you think caused them. For example, typos, mixing up similar images, etc. 

If you didn't make any mistakes, you can type "none".
prompt_mistake.value: One mistake was using the plural version of the word, and then mixing up similar images for most of them, there were a couple that I just completely blanked on because I could only remember the most recent image.

prompt_working_together.value: My partner mostly took the lead but if something jumped out to me right away I would mention it or give other ideas if there was something potentially easier.

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: I suggested to use colours as identifier and the other participant agreed. In the beginning it was enough to recognize the object by one colour but later on it became more complicated so we used 3 colours - hats, hands and boots. In the last round we added shapes to 3 colours so 3 colours would be first 3 words followed by the relevant shape and sometimes the shape also needed further description like small, big or the colour. Fourth round felt hard and we made few mistakes, the first  rounds I don't think we made any mistake. The strategy to use colours was amended on each round as things were getting more complicated so we were adding the labels.

prompt_working_together.value: We quickly agreed. I suggested colours and he accepted as he thought the approach would work. He suggested adding shapes to labels in the 4th round.

# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

Did you make any mistakes in remembering the names you gave to the images?

If so, please describe what you think caused them. For example, typos, mixing up similar images, etc. 

If you didn't make any mistakes, you can type "none".
prompt_mistake.value: No we didnt make mistakes and scored quite well. I think keeping the names simple and naming them after things we both agreed they looked like worked well for us.

prompt_working_together.name: working_together
prompt_working_together.prompt:
# How did you and your partner divide the work of coming up with names?

For example, did you both suggest names, take turns, have one person take the lead, or use some other approach?
prompt_working_together.value: As the objects were mostly abstract we both just spoke up when we had an idea. Often this would trigger a similar thought from the other person and once we both agreed on something we could remember we went with that name.

In the first 3 rounds, we assign colors to body parts from top to bottom (Head → Chest → Arms → Legs → Details). This order is easy to remember and follow.
Once the images become more complex, we switch to creating a short, vivid story or scene based on what the figure looks like. We describe it together as if it's a funny or weird situation.

prompt_strategy.value: Because my partner left at the beginning, I had to act as if he was still there and replicate how we would have agreed to image names and according strategy. It was unfortunate he left, but in theory I acted out in the way I saw his immediate body language. He seemed to me quite introverted, and as I have to lead people at work and in social life, I acted as if I was the leader, but taking on board his input. The strategy used was based on easy names to remember, like identifying colors or stand out features. The strategy stayed the same in this way, as it worked well in the first round. The only disagreement I could have seen is if our preference for identification names differed significantly. With this in mind, the easy solution would have been a compromise and give and take on image name ideas.

prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: Breaking it down to the simplest possible thing, for example, for a figure that had long legs, that was labelled 'legs'. For a figure that was tall, 'tall'. We also seemed to pick the first label we thought of, so if we thought of different labels afterwards we mostly returned to our first one, usually because it had almost already solidified the association. Answers that were funny were easiest to recall, if I wasn't sure during the guessing stage, I'd think, what about this character is amusing? This also helped build rappor between myself and my partner, although this could allow for crude/offensive jokes, but me and my matched partner seemed to work together well. Admittedly there wasn't a discussion about strategy between me and my partner, it formed naturally, we changed tactic only naturally when we figured out what worked from the training rounds.

prompt_working_together.name: working_together
prompt_working_together.prompt:
# How did you and your partner divide the work of coming up with names?

For example, did you both suggest names, take turns, have one person take the lead, or use some other approach?
prompt_working_together.value: We didn't go in order, we both looked at the images as a whole first and in my case, I called out what was most distinctive to me, my partner was from Canada and I'm from the UK and we were slightly different ages, although we likely share plenty of cultural references, there were at least two occasions where we associated an object with a cartoon character or a candy that the other person didn't know, me and my partner discussed this in one case, where a cartoon character I referenced he was not aware of, I suggested we find something we both know but he said he was happy to go with the cartoon character name and assured me he would remember it, which he did.

prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: The strategy I used was to let my partner lead as they had a more visual way of naming. I also made sure to come up with ideas. We took turns so If I named one or two I would say "you pick the next one". I tried to create names based on color or shape or a name easy to remember. I can't believe I got the name one wrong I used my name "[name]" instead of the name "jane" we chose for the object. We had a laugh about that. It was funny because I chose extremely confident in my answer and got it wrong.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake
prompt_mistake.prompt:
# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

Did you make any mistakes in remembering the names you gave to the images?

If so, please describe what you think caused them. For example, typos, mixing up similar images, etc. 

If you didn't make any mistakes, you can type "none".
prompt_mistake.value: Yes I one mistake by labeling the object the alias name, "jane, then when shown the object I put "[name]", my real name.

prompt_working_together.name: working_together
prompt_working_together.prompt:
# How did you and your partner divide the work of coming up with names?

For example, did you both suggest names, take turns, have one person take the lead, or use some other approach?
prompt_working_together.value: my partner [name], did lead as he seemed to have a way of labeling that was easiest for his mind to recall, but we took turns as I would come up with a name and then ask him to go next.
